title: FBR e-Invoicing Pakistan Explained – What Every Business Must Know
metaDescription: Clear explanation of FBR e-invoicing requirements for Pakistan businesses. QR invoice format, submission process, penalties for non-compliance, and how to set it up fast.
content:
What Is FBR e-Invoicing?

FBR e-invoicing is the system by which Pakistani businesses submit their sales invoices electronically to the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) in real time. Unlike traditional paper invoices, e-invoices are transmitted to the FBR's IRIS system the moment a sale is made, creating a live, auditable record of all business transactions.

The centerpiece of this system is the QR code — every FBR e-invoice must include a scannable QR code that customers can use to verify the invoice is genuine and that the business is FBR registered.

The FBR QR Invoice – What It Contains

Every FBR-compliant QR invoice must include the following information:

  • Seller's STRN (Sales Tax Registration Number)
  • Seller's NTN (National Tax Number)
  • Business name and address
  • Invoice date and unique invoice number
  • List of items sold with quantity, unit price, and total
  • Sales tax amount (broken down by applicable rate)
  • Total amount payable
  • QR code linking to FBR invoice verification

Customers who receive a QR invoice can scan the code to verify on the FBR website that the invoice is genuine. This gives customers confidence and protects them from fake receipts.

How e-Invoice Submission Works

When a sale is made through an FBR-integrated POS system, the following happens automatically:

  1. The sale details are captured by the POS software
  2. Sales tax is calculated based on the applicable rate for each item
  3. The invoice is formatted according to FBR requirements
  4. The invoice is transmitted to FBR IRIS via a secure API connection
  5. FBR assigns a unique verification code
  6. A QR code is generated embedding the verification code
  7. The printed or digital receipt is given to the customer

The entire process takes a fraction of a second — from the customer's perspective, it's identical to a normal sale.

Who Must Issue FBR e-Invoices?

As of 2026, the following must issue FBR QR invoices:

  • All Tier-1 retailers as defined by FBR (large turnover businesses)
  • Chain stores and franchises operating multiple branches
  • Pharmacies in designated cities
  • Restaurants and food businesses above the threshold
  • Wholesalers registered for sales tax

FBR has indicated it will extend requirements to smaller businesses progressively. Voluntary early adoption is encouraged and comes with benefits including simplified tax filing.

Penalties for Not Issuing FBR Invoices

Operating without proper FBR invoice integration carries serious consequences:

  • Fines starting at PKR 10,000 per day of non-compliance
  • Penalties of up to PKR 1,000,000 for repeated violations
  • Sales tax registration suspension
  • FBR audit triggers — non-compliant businesses are flagged for full audits
  • Court proceedings in cases of deliberate evasion

Benefits of Going Digital with FBR e-Invoicing

Beyond compliance, businesses that fully adopt FBR e-invoicing gain real operational advantages:

  • Automated tax records – Monthly sales tax returns are pre-filled from your e-invoice data, saving hours of manual work
  • Fraud protection – QR codes make it impossible for employees to pocket cash from unrecorded sales
  • Customer trust – Verifiable invoices signal your business is professional and legitimate
  • Faster audits – If FBR does audit, your complete digital records speed up the process dramatically
  • Business insights – Digital sales data enables better decision-making
